title: Maturity and Due-and-Payable Cases: Resolution Period and Extension Schedule
content:
Each Maturity and Due-and-Payable Cases plan sets the period for resolving a called-due loan, how far one extension carries it, and how many extensions a case may receive.

| Case plan | Resolution period after the due-and-payable date | Days added by one extension | Largest number of extensions on one case |
|---|---|---|---|
| Death of Last Surviving Borrower | 6 calendar months | 90 calendar days | 2 |
| Sale or Title Transfer | 6 calendar months | 90 calendar days | 2 |
| Extended Health-Care Absence | 6 calendar months | 90 calendar days | 2 |
| Principal Residence Change | 6 calendar months | 90 calendar days | 2 |
| Property Charge Default | 6 calendar months | 90 calendar days | 1 |
| Property Condition Default | 6 calendar months | 90 calendar days | 1 |

The following settings are the same under all six plans:

| Setting | Value under every plan |
|---|---|
| Documents that support an extension request | a listing agreement or a financing commitment |
| Each extension needs HUD approval recorded on the case first | yes |
| New appraisal ordered when an extension is granted after the current appraisal has passed its months of usability | yes |
| Days before the current resolution deadline by which an extension request should reach Cedarline, so HUD approval can be sought in time | 15 calendar days |
| Days after the resolution deadline on which the case may first be referred to foreclosure | 1 calendar day |

## Worked reading, hypothetical figures

- A death, sale or occupancy case may receive at most 2 extensions; a property charge or property condition case at most 1.
- One extension adds 90 calendar days to the resolution deadline in force when it is granted. Under any plan, a deadline of an invented 10 May is carried to 8 August.
- The first day of possible referral is the day after the resolution deadline, since the figure is 1 calendar day under every plan.
